'''Paul Eugene Schupp''' (March 12, 1937 – January 24, 2022) was an American-born British [[professor]] [[emeritus]] of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign]]. He is known for his contributions to [[geometric group theory]], [[computational complexity]] and the [[theory of computability]].<ref name="Schupp Biography">{{Cite journal | first1= Ilya |last1= Kapovich | year = 2010 | journal = [[Illinois Journal of Mathematics]] | title = On mathematical contributions of Paul E. Schupp. |volume=54|mr=2776982|pages=1–9|doi= 10.1215/ijm/1299679735 |doi-access= free }}</ref>

He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1966 under the direction of [[Roger Lyndon]].

Together with [[Roger Lyndon]] he is the coauthor of  the book "Combinatorial Group Theory" which provided a comprehensive account of the subject of Combinatorial Group Theory, starting with the work of Dehn in the 1910s and to late 1970s and remains a modern standard for the subject of [[small cancellation theory]].<ref name="Schupp Biography"/> Starting 1980's he worked on problems that explored the connections between [[Group theory]] and [[Computer Science]] and [[Computational complexity theory|Complexity Theory]].  Together with [[David E. Muller|David Muller]] he proved that a [[finitely generated group]] ''G'' has [[context-free language|context-free]] [[Word problem for groups|word problem]] if and only if ''G'' is [[virtually free group|virtually free]], which is now known as [[Muller–Schupp theorem]].<ref name=MS83>David  E. Muller, and Paul E. Schupp, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/002200008390003X ''Groups, the theory of ends, and context-free languages''.] 
[[Journal of Computer and System Sciences]] '''26''' (1983), no. 3, 295–310</ref>

In 1977, Schupp received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]. In 2012, he was named an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. In 2017,  the conference "Groups and Computation" was organized at Stevens Institute of Technology celebrating the mathematical contributions of Paul Schupp.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.stevens.edu/algebraic/Schupp/|title=Conference 'Groups and Computation: Interactions between geometric group theory, computability and computer science'|work=[[Stevens Institute of Technology]]|access-date=2020-04-05}} </ref> Schupp died on January 24, 2022, at the age of 84.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 January 2022 |title=Paul Schupp dead at 84 |url=https://math.illinois.edu/news/2022-02-11t211600/paul-schupp-obituary-and-memorial-service |access-date=22 November 2024}}</ref>
